links.targetTitle: Treasury allocation is a strict waterfall in which no later

title: Backstop capital retention tapers continuously to zero near target but jumps to a flat 50% below the Turbo-Fill Floor
content:
A.2.3.1.2.3 defines three regimes for Step 2 Capital. Below the Turbo-Fill Floor, "fifty percent (50%) of Step 2 Capital is retained to grow Aggregate Backstop Capital." Between the floor and the Target, retention is "fifty percent (50%) multiplied by the fill factor, where the fill factor is one (1) minus the ratio of current Aggregate Backstop Capital to the Target." At or above Target, "none of Step 2 Capital is retained."

The middle regime is a proportional controller: the closer the buffer gets to target, the less revenue it absorbs, reaching zero exactly at target. This avoids the pathology of a hard threshold, where the last dollar of filling would divert half of a month's revenue and crossing the line would swing the payout to stakers abruptly.

The interesting artifact is at the floor. Evaluating the taper formula at the floor gives 50% x (1 − floor/target), which is strictly *less* than the flat 50% applied just below it — so retention drops discontinuously as the buffer recovers past the floor. That kink is intentional and is what "Turbo-Fill" names: below the floor the system fills at maximum rate regardless of how far it has to go, because being under-backstopped is a distinct condition rather than a point on a gradient.

Read as policy, the schedule encodes that solvency has strict priority while under-provisioned, and becomes a tapering claim on revenue once merely incomplete. Note also the cap: retention never exceeds half of Step 2 Capital, so stakers always receive something even in the worst regime.
description: Between floor and target, retention is 50% times one minus the ratio of current to target; below the floor it is a flat 50%, creating a deliberate discontinuity at the floor.
